name: Brazilian citizenship by naturalisation (Lei 13.445/2017, Art. 64-71)

requirements.blocker_text: Requires civil capacity under Brazilian law, indefinite-term residence in Brazil for at least 4 years, communication ability in Portuguese, and no unrehabilitated criminal conviction.
requirements.fix_path: Continue accruing indefinite-term residence until the 4-year threshold is met, and demonstrate Portuguese communication ability.

requirements.blocker_text: The 4-year residency requirement drops to a minimum of 1 year if the applicant has a Brazilian child; has a Brazilian spouse or partner and is not legally or factually separated from them at the time of the grant; has rendered or can render relevant service to Brazil; or is recommended by professional, scientific, or artistic capacity. A separate constitutional provision (distinct from this Article 66 list) reduces the requirement to 1 year of uninterrupted residence plus good moral standing for nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries specifically.
requirements.fix_path: Establish one of the qualifying bases (Brazilian child, Brazilian spouse/partner, relevant service, or professional/scientific/artistic distinction), or rely on Portuguese-speaking-country nationality if applicable.

requirements.blocker_text: Available to any foreign national residing in Brazil for more than 15 uninterrupted years without a criminal conviction, who requests Brazilian nationality -- this constitutional provision (Art. 12, I, 'c' of the Constitution, restated in the Migration Law) requires no other condition beyond residence duration, no criminal record, and the request itself.
requirements.fix_path: Continue accruing uninterrupted residence until the 15-year threshold is met.

requirement_groups.name: Naturalização especial, spouse of Brazilian foreign-service personnel

requirements.blocker_text: Available to the spouse or partner, for more than 5 years, of an active member of the Brazilian Foreign Service or of a person serving Brazil abroad -- requires civil capacity, Portuguese communication ability, and no unrehabilitated criminal conviction, but no separate residence-duration test of its own.

evidence_required.document: Proof of indefinite-term residence (CRNM) for the applicable period
Portuguese-language communication evidence (assessed proportionate to the applicant's circumstances, not a fixed formal exam)
Clean criminal record certificate, or proof of rehabilitation

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: sporadic trips abroad totalling no more than 3 months within a 1-year residence requirement, 6 months within a 2-year requirement, or 12 months within a 4-year requirement do not interrupt the naturalisation clock

sources.title: Câmara dos Deputados (camara.leg.br, official legislative text repository) -- full text of Lei nº 13.445, de 24 de maio de 2017 (Lei de Migração), Articles 64-71 on naturalisation

Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (gov.br/mj) -- official guidance on the residence-period requirement, including the sporadic-absence proportionality rule and the rule that refugee-status applicants count from their CONARE application date

notes: Four genuinely distinct naturalisation mechanisms, correctly modeled as OR-logic groups per this schema's core design decision -- the same four-type structure (ordinária/extraordinária/especial/provisória) is set out explicitly in Lei 13.445/2017 Article 64, an unusually clean match between the statute's own taxonomy and this schema's requirement_groups mechanism. A fourth type, naturalização provisória (for children/adolescents who established Brazilian residence before age 10, applied for via legal representative, converting to definitive status if the naturalised person requests it within 2 years of reaching majority), is not modeled as its own group here since it applies to a fundamentally different applicant profile (minors via representative) than the adult-applicant framing this dataset generally uses -- flagged as a candidate for a future expansion. dual_citizenship_allowed is true throughout, consistent with Brazil's general acceptance of dual nationality (unlike China, Korea's general track, and Saudi Arabia, all of which restrict or bar it in this dataset) -- a genuine structural finding worth surfacing on any cross-country comparison, since Brazil imposes no renunciation requirement on naturalised citizens at all. gov.br/mj's own guidance confirms a favourable detail for br_refugee_status specifically: for CONARE-recognised refugees, the residence-period clock for naturalisation counts from the date of the refugee-status application itself, not from the date of recognition -- meaningfully faster than it might first appear given how long CONARE's process can take. The reduced 1-year track (ordinaria_reduced) combines two textually distinct legal bases that produce the same practical outcome: Article 66's list (Brazilian child, Brazilian spouse/partner, relevant service, professional distinction) and a separate constitutional provision specifically for Portuguese-speaking-country nationals (1 year plus good moral standing, no other condition) -- both collapsed into one requirement_group here since the schema doesn't have a clean way to express 'two different legal articles producing an identical 1-year reduction,' flagged as a simplification consistent with this project's honesty conventions rather than silently treated as one uniform rule.
